battle.name: 隋滅陳之戰
battle.brief: 開皇八年十月，隋文帝下詔伐陳，以晉王楊廣為行軍元帥，楊素領舟師自永安順江而下，韓擒虎、賀若弼率精兵夜渡采石，不足兩月而陳都建康陷落，陳後主藏於景陽殿井中被擒，陳朝覆亡。卡面亞述長弓並未隨軍南下，隋軍壓陣的是蹶張弩與步弓，弓弩齊射、舟車並進，正是亞述弓兵開路、車兵隨行的老路數。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 這場戰爭是南北朝最後一場大規模的王朝戰爭，交戰一方是開皇元年滅北周、控制了北方的隋朝，另一方是南朝末代陳朝，都城在江南的建康。隋軍的指揮體系建立在開皇七年第一次伐陳失敗之後的整頓之上：文帝楊堅以晉王楊廣為行軍元帥，總領諸軍；司空楊素節制自永安出發的西路舟師，順江東下；秦王楊俊統兵在襄漢一線策應；行軍元帥副將王誼率眾經江陵、荊州方向南下，與楊素舟師互相策應；右衛大將軍韓擒虎與撫州總管賀若弼率先鋒渡江，專責直取建康。編制上分舟師、步騎、攻城部隊與力役四類，糧秣主要由汴口沿汴水入淮、接江南運河轉運，隨軍另有工匠修造攻城器械。陳軍則以京口與建康為樞紐，沿長江諸州郡分置守兵，樞密院掌軍籍與調發，鎮東大將軍蕭摩訶、徐州刺史裴忌、荊州刺史淳于量等分守要地，京口精兵與長江水師是其最後依賴。陳朝疆域跨江淮南北與嶺南，士族門第多持觀望態度，北援則因高句麗方面隋軍的牽制而無從指望。
countriesEn: This war was the last large-scale dynastic conflict of the Southern and Northern Dynasties, fought between the Sui, which had destroyed Northern Zhou in 581 and brought the north under its control, and the Chen, the last of the southern dynasties, whose capital was Jiankang on the lower Yangtze. The Sui command system was the one rebuilt after the first campaign against Chen had failed in Kaihuang 7. Emperor Wen, Yang Jian, appointed his son the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, as supreme commander of the expedition; the chancellor Yang Su commanded the western river fleet that set out from Yong'an and came down the river; the Prince of Qin, Yang Jun, operated on the Xiangyang-Han line; the deputy supreme commander Wang Yi led a force south by way of Jiangling and Jingzhou, working in concert with Yang Su's fleet; and the Right Guard commander Han Qinhu together with the governor of Fuzhou, He Ruobi, led the vanguard across the river with the single task of taking Jiankang directly. The order of battle was divided into river forces, infantry and cavalry, siege troops and labour; the grain came chiefly by way of Biankou and the Bian water into the Huai and then by the Jiangnan canal, and engineers travelled with the army to build siege equipment. The Chen armed forces pivoted on Jingkou and Jiankang, with garrisons in the commanderies along the Yangtze, the Directorate of Military Affairs in charge of the registers and the dispatch of troops, and commanders such as the General of the Eastern Army Xiao Mohe, the Inspector of Xu Pei Ji and the Inspector of Jingzhou Chunyu Liang holding the key posts; the elite of the capital and the river fleet were their last reliance. The Chen realm stretched north and south of the river and into Lingnan, the great clans of the south mostly stood aside and watched, and no help from the north was possible, because a Sui army of some three hundred thousand was engaging Goguryeo and holding down that approach.
people: 留下姓名的多數是隋方。隋文帝楊堅在位二十三年，是這場戰爭的決策者：開皇八年十月下詔全面伐陳，並在事先一年完成了造船、練兵與轉運的準備；他讓晉王楊廣出總元帥，是把軍政大權與儲君之位一同交出。楊廣在戰役中坐鎮建康，太子楊勇已被廢、蜀王秀尚幼，隋廷實際上只有他能獨當一面。楊素是此役的西線主帥，也是隋朝最負盛名的統帥：他在益州督造黃龍大艦，率五十一萬眾自永安東下，過三峽時縱火破陳軍阻截，是全軍最艱險的一段。楊俊領兵在襄漢一線策應，王誼為元帥副，率眾自襄陽順流而下，在湖北擊破陳將淳于量。韓擒虎年少驍勇，率五百精兵為夜渡的先鋒之一；賀若弼的奇謀最關鍵：他在廣陵預造商船六十餘艘，夜間換人為隋軍士卒，順流直取采石，身先士卒登上石磯頭。隋廷中蘇威曾以陳有固守之資、兵久疲為由力諫，文帝幾怒而殺之，終究不聽；另一路，隋以高熲為帥率眾三十萬攻高句麗，牽制北境，使陳無外援。陳方留下姓名的有後主陳叔寶、寵妃張麗華與孔貴嬪，散兵大將蕭摩訶、徐州刺史裴忌、荊州刺史淳于量、征虜將軍侯安都與尚書令蔡大寶。蕭摩訶在采石兵敗後退保京口，與賀若弼單騎相遇而一擊不中，終究率殘部降隋；侯安都本擬斷隋軍後路，卻在半途叛降。陳亡後，陳後主被封懷王待遇不薄，太妃樂昌公主與駙馬徐德言的破鏡重圓，則成為此役在民間流傳最久的餘韻。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive belong to the Sui side. Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, reigned for twenty-three years and was the man who decided this war: in the tenth month of Kaihuang 8 he issued the general edict for the campaign, having already completed the building of ships, the training of troops and the arrangement of transport during the year before. He put the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, in the field as supreme commander, handing over the military authority and the position of heir apparent together. Yang Guang sat at Jiankang during the campaign; the crown prince Yang Yong had already been deposed and the Prince of Shu, Yang Xiu, was still a child, so Yang Guang was in practice the only one at the Sui court capable of standing on his own. Yang Su was the commander of the western line and the most celebrated of the Sui commanders: he supervised the building of the great yellow dragon ships in Yizhou, led five hundred and ten thousand men east from Yong'an, and broke the Chen obstruction at the gorges by fire, the hardest passage of the whole campaign. Yang Jun operated with the army on the Xiangyang-Han line, and Wang Yi, deputy to the supreme commander, marched down from Xiangyang and defeated the Chen general Chunyu Liang in Hubei. Han Qinhu was young and fierce and led five hundred picked men as one of the two vanguards of the night crossing. The stratagem that mattered most was He Ruobi's: at Guangling he had sixty-odd merchant ships built in secret, and at night the cargo was struck out and Sui soldiers put in, so that the fleet drifted down the river to take Caishi, He himself among the first to scramble ashore on the Shijitou rocks. In the Sui court Su Wei pressed the emperor not to attack on the ground that Chen still had the resources for a stubborn defence and that the troops would be exhausted by a long campaign; the emperor was close to killing him for it and in the end did not listen. On another front the Sui sent Gao Jiong with a host of three hundred thousand against Goguryeo, which pinned down the northern approach and left Chen without reinforcement. On the Chen side the names recorded are the last emperor, Chen Shubao, his favoured consorts Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei, the general Xiao Mohe, the Inspector of Xu Pei Ji, the Inspector of Jingzhou Chunyu Liang, the General of Remonstrant Host Hou Andu and the director of the secretariat Cai Dabao. After the defeat at Caishi, Xiao Mohe fell back on Jingkou, and the story goes that he met He Ruobi single-handed, struck at him and missed, and finally led his remnants over to the Sui. Hou Andu, who was to have cut the Sui supply line, defected on the way instead. After the fall of Chen the last emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Huai and treated with some care, and the reunion of the Tai-fei, the Princess Lechang, with her husband Xu Deyan became the longest-lived trace this campaign left in popular memory.
kits: 先把一件容易誤讀的事說清楚：卡面上的亞述長弓並沒有隨隋軍南下。亞述弓是公元前九世紀以降亞述軍隊的骨幹兵器：木胎為芯，弓背貼牛角、弓腹貼牛筋，弦用牛筋或羊腸，弓身約臂長有餘，配三棱或柳葉形鐵鏃，箭羽取鵲鷹翎；亞述王宮的浮雕裡，弓兵成排齊射的場面反覆出現，亞述君主慣於在城頭觀看自家箭雨落在敵陣，亞述人的國號因此被說成「亞述的箭」。卡面簡介裡那句「弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路」，說的正是亞述戰車兵本身不善獨立作戰，車陣的推進依賴前導弓手的壓制。放到隋滅陳的裝備表裡，亞述長弓代表的是「以弓弩齊射壓制、再以車舟承載衝力」這一類技術路線的祖型，而隋軍真正握在手裡的，是一套成熟得多、也殘酷得多的東西。遠射主力是弩：蹶張弩以木為臂，機括用金屬，射手需以足踏或以腰力張弦，發射遲緩而射程遠、精度高，步軍以之封鎖江面與城頭；弓則為輔，單兵攜帶便利，發射快，適合追擊、騷擾與近距離急速射。隋軍舟師在每條船前列弩手，專射岸上陳軍與陳軍戰船上的舵手與執纖者；岸上攻城部隊同樣以弩壓制城頭。陳軍在城上造巢車，高十餘丈以觀隋軍營壘，被隋軍弓弩射擊，死者甚眾，這是亞述弓兵與隋弩兵隔著一千二百年之後的一次遙遙對照。攻城另有覆布車與攻城車：車上蒙布與牛皮，推至城下，兵人自車上射擊、燒敵，減少矢石之害。舟師的戰術器材則是火：火炬、油瓶與薪柴，用來在江面縱火，破陳軍舟船。開皇七年隋軍第一次伐陳之所以全軍潰敗，正是因為舟船在峽中被陳軍火攻燒毀，士卒死者十居七八；隋朝八年之後在舟船上備水備火桶、與友軍舟船錯開停泊，正是針對這一段教訓的補課。鞍馬方面，隋軍以牛馬馭車運糧，士卒負三日口糧自隨，另賴運河與運糧的船隊維持遠距離補給。陳軍除江防舟師與巢車外，據《隋書》所記還備有木製的櫓盾與長槊，用以抵禦隋軍登岸的衝鋒。
kitsEn: One thing has to be said first, because it is easy to misread: the Assyrian bow on the card did not march south with the Sui army. The Assyrian bow was the backbone weapon of the Assyrian army from the ninth century BC onward: a wooden core faced with horn on the back and sinew on the belly, a string of sinew or gut, a body a little over the length of a man's arm, and it was used with trilobed or willow-leaf iron heads and quivers of kite and eagle feathers. In the reliefs of the Assyrian royal palaces the rows of archers shooting in unison recur constantly; Assyrian kings were accustomed to watching from the ramparts the fall of their own arrow-fall on the enemy, and the empire's very name came to be glossed as the arrow of Assyria. The line on the card's own description, that archers shot from the chariots and the chariots relied on the archers to open the way, describes precisely the Assyrian chariot troops, who were not good at fighting independently: the advance of the chariot line depended on the suppression worked by the leading bowmen. Placed in the equipment table of the Sui conquest of Chen, the Assyrian bow stands for the ancestor type of a line of technique in which the bow-shot line suppresses and the chariot and the boat carry the shock afterwards. What the Sui army actually held in its hands was a far more mature and far more brutal set of things. The backbone of its missile power was the crossbow: the drawn crossbow had a wooden stock, a metal lock, and the shooter had to span the string with foot or hip, so it was slow to fire but far-reaching and accurate, and the infantry used it to seal the river and the walls. The bow itself was secondary, convenient to carry, quick to shoot, and suited to pursuit, harassment and rapid shooting at close range. The Sui river fleet posted crossbowmen along the foredeck of every vessel, whose business was the Chen troops on the bank and the helmsmen and cable-haulers of the Chen ships; the siege troops ashore used the same weapon to dominate the walls. The Chen built nest-towers on the city walls, over ten zhang high, from which they observed the Sui camp, and they were shot down by Sui bows and crossbows with heavy loss among the men who manned them: that was a remote counterpart, across some twelve centuries, of the Assyrian bowmen and the Sui crossbowmen. For the siege there were also cloth-covered vehicles and assault towers: covered with cloth and hide, they were pushed up to the walls, from which the troops shot and fired at the enemy and so reduced the harm done by arrows and stones. The tactical material of the river fleet was fire: torches, oil jars and firewood, used to set fire to the river and destroy the Chen boats. The reason the Sui army was routed in its first campaign against Chen in Kaihuang 7 was precisely that its ships were burned by the Chen fire attack in the gorges, with seven or eight men in ten of the Sui force killed; the eight years of preparation that followed, with water and fire buckets kept aboard and ships berthed apart from one another, were a direct answer to that lesson. For transport the Sui used oxen and horses to draw the grain carts, the soldiers carried three days' rations on their own persons, and the canal and the grain fleets sustained the long-range supply. On the Chen side, besides the river defence and the nest-towers, the records of the Suishu describe wooden shields and long spears intended to hold off the Sui assault on the beach.
tactics: 整場戰爭可以分成三條平行推進的路線，最後在南京城下合攏。東路是奇襲：開皇八年冬，賀若弼在廣陵暗中造商船六十餘艘，每船可容五六十人，平日載貨，藏兵於艙中；夜裡拆去貨艙、換上隋軍士卒，順流東下，在采石一帶登岸。同時韓擒虎率五百精兵為後援，兩部在石磯頭附近得手，陳軍前哨崩潰，裴忌大敗，蕭摩訶的兵也支持不住，隋軍由此取得長江兩岸的立足點，直趨京口，陳軍沿江望風而潰，隋軍追奔至京口，江防門戶洞開。中路是水陸並行：王誼率眾自襄陽、荊州方向沿江而下，在湖北擊破淳于量的部眾，與楊素的舟師互相策應，把陳在長江中游的兵力釘在原地，無法北援京口。西路是楊素的舟師自永安順流東下，過瞿塘、巫、西陵三峽，峽道狹窄，陳軍倚險扼守，隋軍一面以強弩壓制峽口，一面具黃龍大艦、舟船連為浮橋以濟兵糧，一面順流縱火焚燒陳軍舟楫，突破後一路直抵姑孰。糧秣與補給是這場戰爭能速戰速決的前提：隋文帝在開皇八年之前就大修運河，汴水入淮、江南河渠相通，江北之粟可以順流直達采石；舟師自帶百日之糧，騎兵與步卒則以隨軍輜重車隊輸送。三路合流之後，京口之戰只用了數日：賀若弼自西南雨花台逼近城牆，韓擒虎自北面新林登岸攻城，陳軍主力前此已耗於采石與京口，防守兵力不足，隋軍以覆布車抵近城下、弩手封鎖城頭射孔，陳後主與張麗華、孔貴嬪退入景陽殿，藏入枯井，隋軍呼之不應、索繩引之乃出，陳朝至此而亡。整體作戰邏輯是典型的隋式：不求野戰決勝，而是以舟師工程、奇襲渡江與對陳內部的分化，一步步把優勢轉化為殲滅性結果。
tacticsEn: The whole campaign can be divided into three parallel lines of advance that finally closed together below the walls of Jiankang. The eastern line was a surprise: in the winter of Kaihuang 8 He Ruobi had sixty-odd merchant ships built in secret at Guangling, each able to hold fifty or sixty men, carrying cargo by day and hiding soldiers in the holds; at night the cargo was struck out, Sui soldiers put in, and the fleet drifted down the river to land in the neighbourhood of Caishi. At the same moment Han Qinhu brought up five hundred picked men as support, and the two parties got their footing at the Shijitou rocks, where the Chen outpost collapsed, Pei Ji was defeated and Xiao Mohe's troops could not hold; the Sui thus gained a bridgehead on both banks of the river and drove straight for Jingkou, the Chen forces along the river breaking at the sight of them, and the Sui pursuing them as far as Jingkou, which left the river defence wide open. The middle line moved by land and water together: Wang Yi came down from the Xiangyang and Jingzhou direction along the river, beat Chunyu Liang's troops in Hubei, worked in concert with Yang Su's fleet and pinned the Chen forces in the middle Yangtze in place, unable to march to the relief of Jingkou. The western line was Yang Su's fleet, which set out from Yong'an and drifted down the river past the three gorges of Qutang, Wu and Xiling; the gorge roads were narrow and the Chen held the heights, and the Sui pressed the gorge mouths with heavy crossbows, lashed their great yellow dragon ships and other craft into a floating bridge to carry troops and grain, and at the same time sent fire down the stream to burn the Chen boats, breaking through and pressing on to Gusu. Supply was the precondition of a war fought this fast: before Kaihuang 8 the Sui had already cut and improved the canals, so that the Bian water fed into the Huai and the Jiangnan channels connected with it, and the grain of the north bank could drift down as far as Caishi; the fleet carried a hundred days' provisions, and the cavalry and foot depended on the baggage trains that marched with them. Once the three lines had joined, the battle of Jingkou took only a few days: He Ruobi came up against the wall from the south-west at Yuhuatai, Han Qinhu landed and attacked from the north at Xinlin, the Chen main force having already been spent at Caishi and Jingkou and the garrison too thin to hold; the Sui brought the cloth-covered vehicles up to the foot of the wall and the crossbowmen closed the firing slits of the wall, and the last emperor with Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei withdrew into the Hall of the Rising Sun and hid in a dry well, where the Sui soldiers called out to them and, getting no answer, drew them up on a rope. Chen perished there. The whole logic is characteristically Sui: no attempt to win a battle in the open field, but the conversion of a superiority into a crushing result by means of river engineering, a surprise crossing and the playing on of divisions inside Chen.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類。年月最為確定：隋文帝於開皇八年（公元588年）十月下詔伐陳，開皇九年（公元589年）正月，韓擒虎、賀若弼夜渡采石，隋軍入京口，同月兵臨建康，陳都於次月陷落；換成西曆，渡江在公元589年1月底，陳亡在589年2月，與《資治通鑑》所記的二月相合。兵員方面，《資治通鑑》記楊素領眾五十一萬、戰船千餘艘，數目包括隨軍夫役與漕運人夫，實際作戰兵力遠少於此；賀若弼預造的商船六十餘艘、每船藏五六十人，加上韓擒虎的五百精兵，先鋒渡江的兵不過數千人。陳軍總數無確數，一般推估在數十萬，多數是徵發的州郡兵與水軍。開皇七年隋軍首攻陳朝，兵敗洞口，《資治通鑑》記隋軍士卒死者十居七八，士氣損失慘重，這一役之後隋朝改弦更張，才有開皇八年的傾國之舉。距離與速度可從江程推：自采石至京口、建康，水路約二百餘里；自渡江至陳都陷落，前後不足兩月，兵貴神速在這一役中不是修辭而是算術。隋軍糧食的規模則與運河直接相關：開皇四年（584年）隋開永濟渠，貫通黃河與淮水，開皇八年又大修江南河渠，於是江淮之粟可以抵達江表。另一條同期的數字屬於北方戰線：開皇九年隋以高熲為將，率眾三十萬出師攻高句麗，一度直抵涿水與鴨綠水一帶，攻平壤不下，次年高句麗遣使請降。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several kinds. The dates are the most certain: the Sui emperor issued the general edict in the tenth month of Kaihuang 8, that is 588 AD; in the first month of Kaihuang 9, 589 AD, Han Qinhu and He Ruobi crossed at Caishi in the night, the Sui entered Jingkou in the same month, stood before Jiankang, and the Chen capital fell in the month following. Turned into the western calendar, the crossing came at the end of January 589 and the fall of Chen in February 589, in agreement with the second month recorded in the Zizhi Tongjian. On the strength of men: the Tongjian records Yang Su leading five hundred and ten thousand men and a thousand odd warships, a figure that includes the servants and the boatmen of the transport, so that the actual fighting force was far smaller; He Ruobi's sixty-odd merchant ships carried fifty or sixty men each, and with Han Qinhu's five hundred picked men the force that crossed the river numbered only a few thousand. No exact figure exists for the Chen army, and the general estimate is several tens of thousands, most of them levies from the commanderies and the river fleet. In Kaihuang 7 the Sui army attacked Chen for the first time and was beaten at Dongkou, the Tongjian recording that seven or eight Sui soldiers in ten were killed, a very heavy loss of morale; only after that defeat did the Sui change its approach and prepare the general campaign of Kaihuang 8. Distance and speed can be read off the river: from Caishi to Jingkou and Jiankang the water road is about two hundred li; from the crossing to the fall of the capital, less than two months passed, and the old saying that speed is precious was in this campaign arithmetic rather than rhetoric. The scale of the Sui grain supply is tied directly to the canals: in Kaihuang 4, 584 AD, the Sui cut the Yongji canal linking the Yellow River to the Huai, and in Kaihuang 8 the Jiangnan channels were worked on again, so that the grain of the Huai and the river could reach the far bank of the Yangtze. Another set of contemporary figures belongs to the northern front: in Kaihuang 9 the Sui sent Gao Jiong with three hundred thousand men against Goguryeo, driving as far as the Zhuoshui and the Yalu, failing to take Pyongyang, and in the following year Goguryeo sent an envoy to sue for peace.
cause: 打起來的原因有四層。最外一層是王朝的版圖：隋朝於開皇元年滅北周、控制了北方，又在開皇七年第一次伐陳兵敗洞口之後，確認南朝並非虛弱可欺，只有完成這一戰，才能把南北分立的格局徹底了結。開皇七年那一敗反而成了催化：蕭摩訶以火攻焚燒隋軍舟船，隋軍死者十居七八，文帝由此明白，陳朝的憑據不是城池而是長江，所以此後一年他不做急攻，而是造大艦、練水軍、通運河、備糧秣，把戰爭從一場會戰改成一次工程。第二層是陳朝內部的崩壞。陳後主寵信張麗華、孔貴嬪，怠於政事，捐國帑修造景陽殿，江南士族多有怨望；將領之間互不信任，陳的援軍屢屢在途中遲滯，裴忌新敗即奔、侯安都甚至叛降隋朝。第三層是隋的國力：開皇年間休養之後，府庫充盈，糧食足而兵精，運河把江北剩餘一路運到江表，徵發的民夫與工匠可以支撐一支龐大的水陸並行大軍。第四層是時機與戰略的湊巧：春汛水漲，楊素的舟師可以順流東下，不必像開皇七年那樣在峽中被人燒船；同時隋以三十萬眾攻高句麗，陳的外援之路被掐斷，而隋對陳的策略不是硬碰，而是東路奇襲與西路強攻同時壓上，讓陳無法判斷主攻方向。隋文帝把出兵的時機選在開皇九年正月，既避開了陳方可能的秋防，也利用了江南冬季水文的便利。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause behind the fighting. The outermost is the map of the dynasty: the Sui had destroyed Northern Zhou in Kaihuang 1 and taken control of the north, and after the first campaign against Chen had been beaten at Dongkou in Kaihuang 7 it knew that the southern court was not so weak as to be taken lightly; only this war could bring the long division of north and south to an end. That defeat of Kaihuang 7 turned out to be a catalyst: Xiao Mohe burned the Sui river fleet with fire, seven or eight Sui men in ten were killed, and the emperor understood at once that the strength of Chen lay not in its cities but in the Yangtze. So for a year afterwards he did not press the attack; he built great ships, trained river troops, opened canals and stored grain, turning a battle into an engineering works. The second layer is the collapse inside Chen. The last emperor favoured Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei, neglected business, and spent the resources of the state on the Hall of the Rising Sun; the great clans of the south had much reason for resentment, the commanders did not trust one another, and the Chen relief forces were repeatedly late on the road, Pei Ji breaking and running at once after his defeat and Hou Andu actually defecting to the Sui. The third layer is the strength of the Sui state: after the rest of Kaihuang the treasuries were full, the grain ample and the troops well found, the canals carried the surplus of the north bank as far as the far shore, and the conscripted labour and craftsmen could support an enormous army moving by land and river together. The fourth layer is the coincidence of timing and strategy: the spring floods were up, so Yang Su's fleet could run down the river instead of being burned in the gorges as in Kaihuang 7; at the same time a Sui army of three hundred thousand was engaging Goguryeo and Chen's road to northern help was cut off; and the Sui plan was not to collide head-on but to press with a surprise in the east and a forcing of the gorges in the west at once, so that Chen could not tell which was the main effort. The Sui emperor chose to move in the first month of Kaihuang 9, which avoided the autumn defence Chen might have prepared and took advantage of the winter conditions of the Jiangnan waterways.
impact: 此役的後果，最深的一層是政治版圖。公元589年陳朝覆亡，東晉十六國以來近三百年的南北分立告一段落，隋成為中國第二個大一統王朝，其統治範圍東至東海、西抵西域、南盡嶺南、北盡大漠，疆域規模在當時前所未有。制度層面，隋朝在陳的廢墟上建立起延續三百年的帝國框架：三省制的定型、尚書省六部的職掌劃分、州縣兩級的行政、對邊疆的羈縻與都護府體制，都在此後由隋入唐而成型；開皇年間的取士之法——開皇七年詔令諸州舉秀才，開皇十八年又下詔令五品以上官員以志行修偉為秀才——被後世視為科舉制度的開端，門閥壟斷官位的局面自此被撬開，江南舊族與北方新貴同場競逐，這是陳亡之後才出現的政治局面。江南社會本身也經歷震盪：陳朝的士族大族失去了政權與軍權，大量陳遺民北遷或流亡，樂昌公主與徐德言的破鏡重圓、《玉樹後庭花》被後人譜成亡國之音，都是這一時期留下的文化印記。物質層面最巨大的工程是運河：隋文帝開皇四年已開永濟渠，隋煬帝大業元年再通江、淮、江南、河道，令南北漕運連成一體，而此役所消耗的江南財力與兵源，恰恰是先帝留下的；楊廣即位後三征高句麗、濫用民力，天下由是大亂，隋朝在統一之後僅存二十九年，隨之而來的唐朝則在隋的制度骨架上重建秩序。於是這一役既是終結，也是開端：它終結了分裂，卻也把一個新王朝的積累與急躁一併傳了下去。
impactEn: The deepest consequence of this campaign lay in the political map. When Chen fell in 589 AD, the division of north and south that had lasted for close on three hundred years since the Eastern Jin and the Sixteen Kingdoms came to an end, and the Sui became the second unified dynasty in Chinese history, ruling from the eastern sea to the western marches, from Lingnan in the south to the great deserts in the north, over a territory without precedent in the age. At the level of institutions, the Sui built on the ruins of Chen the framework of an empire that would last three hundred years: the fixing of the three departments, the division of functions among the six ministries of the Department of State Affairs, the two-tier administration of commandery and county, and the frontier system of indirect rule and protectorates all took their shape as the Sui handed them to the Tang. The method of selecting officials in the Kaihuang years, the edict of Kaihuang 7 ordering the commanderies to recommend xiucai and the edict of Kaihuang 18 ordering officials of the fifth rank and above to recommend men of notable character, is regarded by later ages as the opening of the examination system, and the monopoly of office by the great families was levered open; old southern clans and new northern men competed on the same ground, and that political situation only became possible after the fall of Chen. Jiangnan society itself was shaken: the great families of Chen lost both the government and the army, large numbers of Chen people moved north or fled, and the reunion of the Princess Lechang with Xu Deyan and the melody later set to the Yu Shu Hou Ting Hua as the song of a lost state are the cultural marks left by that time. On the material side the greatest work was the canal: the Sui emperor Wen had already cut the Yongji canal in Kaihuang 4, and the Yangdi emperor in the first year of Daye opened the connections through the river, the Huai, the Jiangnan and the Lingqu so that the northern and southern grain routes became one; the wealth and the manpower of the south consumed by this campaign were precisely what the former emperor had left behind. After Yang Guang took the throne, three campaigns against Goguryeo and the abuse of the labour of the people threw the realm into disorder, and the Sui survived only twenty-nine years after the unification, while the Tang that followed rebuilt order on the Sui's institutional frame. This campaign was therefore both an end and a beginning: it ended the division, and passed on together with it the accumulation and the impatience of a new dynasty.
result: 公元589年二月，隋軍攻入建康，陳後主陳叔寶與張麗華、孔貴嬪在景陽殿的枯井中被擒獲，陳朝至此而亡，陳的州郡、將士、府庫、版籍盡歸隋室。隋文帝隨後詔封陳後主為懷王，待遇頗為優厚，陳降軍一律收編入隋軍編制，陳的州縣官吏多仍舊任。傳世記載中最著名的一段，是陳後主在隋廷宴席上盛稱江南地廣物豐、稻米支給皆足，隋文帝應以天下方安、須養蒼生之語，兩相比照，一個王朝的末路與另一個王朝的自我期許同時被寫在史冊上。隋朝隨即整頓江南：罷除陳末的苛捐雜賦，合併州縣，重新編定戶籍，遣官鎮撫，並在開皇末年大興屯田水利。就此役本身的技術層面而言，隋朝的取勝可以歸納為三點：以開皇七年敗績為鑑，耗一年時間把舟師與糧秣整備到足以順流攻擊的程度；以西路楊素的水軍配合東路韓擒虎、賀若弼的奇襲渡江，使陳朝無法集中兵力；以北方高句麗戰線牽制陳的外援，再用一場夜渡和兩月的推進把一個尚有兩百餘萬人口的南朝壓垮。陳亡後，中原門第在江南的舊有勢力並未隨之盡滅，隋朝對江表的有效控制其實只維持了數十年，江南的反抗最終匯入隋末唐初的亂局；同時，《玉樹後庭花》被後人譜成亡國之音，讓這場戰爭在記憶裡獲得了一個比任何戰術細節都更長久的形狀。
resultEn: In the second month of 589 AD the Sui army entered Jiankang, and the last emperor, Chen Shubao, together with Zhang Lihua and Kong Guifei, was taken from the dry well of the Hall of the Rising Sun; Chen perished there, and the commanderies, the soldiers, the treasuries and the registers of Chen passed entire to the Sui house. The Sui emperor then enfeoffed the last emperor as Prince of Huai and treated him with a good deal of care; the surrendered troops of Chen were taken into the Sui order of battle, and the commandery and county officials of Chen were largely left in their posts. The most famous passage in the received record is the last emperor's at a banquet of the Sui court, praising the breadth and richness of the south and how ample were its rice rations, and the Sui emperor answering that the realm had only just been brought to peace and that the people must be given a living; set side by side, the end of one dynasty and the self-expectation of another were written into the annals at once. The Sui then set the south in order: the harsh levies and miscellaneous exactions of late Chen were abolished, commanderies and counties were merged, the registers of households were compiled afresh, officials were sent to hold the peace, and in the last years of Kaihuang tilling and waterworks were greatly encouraged. As to the technical side of the campaign itself, the Sui victory can be reduced to three things: taking the defeat of Kaihuang 7 as its lesson and spending a year bringing the river force and the grain up to a standard that allowed an attack with the current; using the river army of Yang Su in the west together with the surprise crossing of Han Qinhu and He Ruobi in the east, so that Chen could not concentrate its forces; and holding down the northern approach with the Goguryeo front, and then bringing down a southern state of more than two million people with one night crossing and two months of advance. After the fall of Chen the old strength of the great northern families in the south did not disappear with it, and the Sui control of the far bank of the river in fact held for only a few decades, the resistance of the south finally feeding into the disorder of the last years of the Sui and the first of the Tang; at the same time the Yu Shu Hou Ting Hua was set to music as the song of a lost state, which gave this war in memory a shape longer-lasting than any tactical detail.
